sharedRules.name: Component
sharedRules.description: Component Teams use the ratings of their parent Unit.

sharedRules.name: Stabiliser
sharedRules.description: Weapons with Stabiliser suffer a +1 penalty To Hit if the Tank Moved in the Movement Step.

sharedRules.name: Smooth Ride
sharedRules.description: M4 Easy Eight Tank teams do not suffer the +1 penalty To Hit for Stabiliser if they Move less than 4”/10cm in the Movement Step.

sharedRules.name: Battle Tank
sharedRules.description: In missions with Deep Reserves, this unit is a Battle Tank Unit. You may only field one Tank Unit with Battle Tank, one Tank Unit with Front Armour of 4 or more, or one Aircraft Unit on table at the start of the game.

sharedRules.name: Seek, Strike, and Destroy
sharedRules.description: A Unit with Seek, Strike, and Destroy may attempt a Shoot and Scoot Movement Order after succeeding in a Blitz Move Movement Order earlier in the same turn.

sharedRules.name: Airborne
sharedRules.description: This Formation may make an Airborne Assault in missions that use the Airborne Assault rules (page 96).

sharedRules.name: MG Transport
sharedRules.description: M1917 HMG or M1919 LMG teams may fire while Mounted as a Passenger in an M3 half-track, using the Optional Passenger MG weapons line.

sharedRules.name: Unit Transport
sharedRules.description: The Unit Leader of the Transport Attachment must end the Movement Step within 6”/15cm of the Unit Leader of its Passenger Unit while on table. If it cannot do this, then the Transport Attachment must be Sent to the Rear.

sharedRules.name: Air Observation Post
sharedRules.description:
An Air Observation Post is an Aircraft that arrives on a roll of 3+ (rather than the usual 4+).

An Air Observation Post is unarmed, but can act as an Observer, Spotting for an Artillery Bombardment with an Aiming Point within 12”/30cm of the Aircraft. The opposing player may shoot at the Aircraft immediately before it rolls to Range In, as though the aircraft was Shooting.

sharedRules.name: Bombs and Rockets
sharedRules.description: (see the Bombs rule on page 93 Flames Of War rulebook)

sharedRules.name: Gigantic
sharedRules.description: Teams from this Unit cannot be placed from Ambush within 16”/40cm of any enemy Team.

sharedRules.name: Rear Firing
sharedRules.description: Rear Firing weapons can only target Teams fully to the rear of the shooting Team, and can only fire an Artillery Bombardment if the Aiming Point is fully to the rear of the shooting Team.

characteristics.$text: Tank telephones were another field modification that saw a lot of use in the dense Bocage hedgerows of Normandy. There telephone boxes were welded to the back of the tank and gave the infantry a direct line of communication with the tank's commander. This greatly improved tank-infantry coordination on the battlefield

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text:
Major Cook jumped into Holland at DZ 'O' near the Maas-Waal Canal. After helping to secure the canal crossing. Cook and his men marched to Nijmegen. There, General Gavin ordered a daylight crossing of the Waal River to outflank the stubborn German defenders entrenched around the city's important bridges.
Cook was given command of the crossing and led his men in the first was across the river.
Once ashone, cook and hhis men cleared the river bank and assaulted both the railroad and highway bridges. After a sharp flight the 3rd Battalion, at 1900 hours, captured the bridge

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text:
During Market Garden Gavin's 82nd Airborne Division quickly secured the Grave bridge.
His next priority was to secure the Groesbeek Heights to protect his flank. However, when he finally turned his attention to Nijmegen the Germans had heavily reinforced the town. 
When the British 30 Corps arrived, Gavin implemented a bold river assualt on 20 September to capture the Nijmegen bridges . The plan was a success and by dawn the next day, 30 Corps was back on the road to Arnhem

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: When he was given the plan for Market Garden, general Maxwell Taylor knew that his 101st Airbourne Division was going to need to hold a rather large portion of the highway open for the British 30 Corps. To deal with this, he gave each of his regiments a point along the highway to another their defences upon. From these strongpoints the division would launch spoiling attacks against the Germans, keeping them occupied while 30 Corps charged north

characteristics.$text: Hyper-velocity armour-piercing (HVAP) ammunition was issued to US tank and anti-tank units from late 1944. This anti-tank projectile has a core of a high-density hard tungsten carbide, surrounded by a shell of a lighter aluminium alloy. The kinectic energy of the round is concentrated in the heavier core into a smaller impact area, improving the round's armour penetration
